question: Can a learned sequential controller construct correct new arithmetic functions, and does any gain justify its complete cost?

data.final_split_access: Do not run model inference on final tasks until the recipe, runtime and development choices have a separate frozen receipt.

learning.supervision: Generator-witness actions with observed partial-program execution; training tasks only.
learning.development_limit: At most three declared recipes on the dev split before a fresh scope decision; retain every attempt. Final measurements cannot guide recipe selection.

evaluation.failure_policy: Retain failures, premature stops, budget exhaustion and invalid actions. Stop search on first explicit neural STOP whose graph meets observed rows; only then check held rows and identity.

decision_rules.learning: At primary cap, each trained ANN seed must exceed its untrained ANN and random-action acceptance rates by at least 0.10. This is a construction-learning gate, not an efficiency claim.
decision_rules.cost: Require observed full coverage for the compared configurations. At their first listed full-coverage caps, standalone ANN per-task CPU including its full setup/fit charge amortized over 244 tasks must be at most 0.90 times streaming. Missing full coverage fails the cost gate.
decision_rules.snn: Report matched SNN accuracy, cost and activity independently. No SNN advantage inferred from parameter counts or binary activity.
decision_rules.scope: Failure does not authorize scaling, new backends or a new final-set tuning pass. Retain the result and diagnose or stop the approach.
